data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol is an epidemic gossip layer that gathers causal null-witnesses for evidence absence; it must durably record the problem ID, the deterministic evidence hash that would have been expected, and a quorum of signed, timestamped null-attestations from distinct nodes.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A network partition isolates the subset of nodes that completed the evidence, allowing the remaining majority to falsely attest null.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Clock drift exceeds the causal horizon, accepting stale nulls after evidence was actually completed moments later.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The deterministic invariant is violated by environment-specific entropy (e.g., timing, random number generation), causing the expected hash to mismatch legitimate evidence.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Because the workspace and thus the evidence are deterministic, any completed result has a fixed content hash. Workspace holders periodically sign and gossip a summary vector of (problem ID, evidence hash or null). Reclamation requires collecting f+1 distinct, correctly signed null vectors from different nodes within a bounded causal horizon. The durable record binds these attestations to the problem ID. Causally, if evidence had been completed, at least one node would have observed the non-null hash during anti-entropy and refused to sign a null attestation. Silent displacement is prevented because the reclamation decision is socially witnessed and the evidence hash is deterministic, making hiding completed evidence equivalent to withholding a quorum.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
